sources.label: W3C IndexedDB API (Recommendation) — the unchanged web API this page's example uses

inventory.name: IndexedDB SQLite backend — storage-engine replacement with the web API unchanged

syntax.rationale: The feature adds no grammar, interface or flag surface of its own ('API change: None — internal implementation only', #at-a-glance; the record's feature_type is 'No developer-visible change'), so the declaration surface this page documents is the unchanged IndexedDB call forms shown in this section's code: indexedDB.open(name, version), db.createObjectStore(name, { keyPath, autoIncrement }), store.createIndex(name, keyPath, { unique }), db.transaction(store, mode) and objectStore.add(value). The only developer-facing control anywhere on the page is the enablement flag in the warning block, which sits above the sections and is recorded in notes. Same ruling as the B3 android-ime unit: when a change has no new grammar, the call forms in the example block are the syntax surface.

inputs.rationale: The inputs are the unchanged call arguments the example passes: the database name and version ('mydb', 1) to open, the keyPath/autoIncrement and unique options to createObjectStore/createIndex, the transaction scope and mode ('items', 'readwrite'), and the record object added ({ name, price }). The backend swap introduces no new input and changes none; the W3C Recommendation defines these same arguments for the API the page says is unchanged.

outputs.rationale: The outputs are the unchanged request/event surfaces the example consumes: request.onupgradeneeded and onsuccess fire, e.target.result yields the IDBDatabase, and tx.oncomplete fires when the transaction commits. The feature exposes no new output to script; the page's point is that these behave identically before and after the engine swap ('Everything above works identically before and after the SQLite migration').

errors.rationale: The page documents no error or exception path for the backend change: its only failure-shaped text is the reliability row ('Improved crash recovery due to SQLite's WAL (write-ahead log) and ACID transaction model'), which describes a recovery improvement rather than an error contract, and the migration row's 'No developer action needed'. The unchanged API's existing error events (request.onerror, IDBDatabase exceptions) are not shown anywhere on this page. FLAGGED GAP, not a claim that no error surface exists: recorded in notes for the implementer.

context.rationale: The at-a-glance table fixes the exposure context: 'Status in 149: In developer trial (behind a flag)', 'Ships by default: Chrome 150', 'API change: None — internal implementation only', and the standards-position row 'Firefox: Shipped · Safari: Shipped (both already use SQLite for IDB)'. The live record corroborates the cross-engine half exactly: its ff view reads 'Shipped/Shipping' with notes 'Firefox uses SQLite for IndexedDB.' and its safari view reads 'Shipped/Shipping' with notes 'Safari uses SQLite for IndexedDB.' (fetched 2026-10-07). The Chrome-milestone half of this fragment is the side of the divergences recorded in notes.

lifecycle.rationale: The lifecycle the page states is a storage-state transition plus a rollout timeline: the Data migration row says 'Chrome migrates existing IDB data automatically on first run of 149. No developer action needed', and the at-a-glance table carries the trial-to-default timeline ('In developer trial (behind a flag)' in 149, 'Ships by default: Chrome 150'). Nothing is constructed or torn down in script. The migration row is the page's side of a carried disagreement — the live record's summary says existing LevelDB data is unimpacted in this step and migration is a later step 3 — recorded in notes, not adjudicated here.

examples.rationale: The page's single complete <pre><code> example: open a database at version 1, create an object store with a keyPath/autoIncrement in the upgradeneeded handler, create an index, then in onsuccess open a readwrite transaction, add a record, and log on transaction complete — followed by the statement that it 'works identically before and after the SQLite migration'. Every call it makes is defined by the linked W3C IndexedDB Recommendation.

compatibility.rationale: The browser-support table lists Chrome '149 — SQLite backend', Edge '149 (Chromium)', Firefox 'SQLite backend (already)' and Safari 'SQLite backend (already)'. The live record corroborates the Firefox and Safari rows (both views 'Shipped/Shipping' with the SQLite notes quoted under context) and corroborates a 149 developer trial via its stage_type 330 stage carrying desktop_first/android_first 149 (fetched 2026-10-07). The page's 'Ships by default: Chrome 150' claim and the table's flat '149 — SQLite backend' phrasing diverge from the record's ship stage (stage_type 360, desktop/android/webview_first all 156, status 'Proposed') — both sides recorded in notes, neither adjudicated.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page documents no security or privacy surface: the change is internal to storage (no new permission, origin, prompt, or script-readable surface), and the closest relevant row is the quota row ('Same quota limits apply. SQLite overhead is minimal'), which is a storage-limit statement, not a security contract. FLAGGED GAP, not a clean absolution: the live record's security_review_status and privacy_review_status both read 'Pending' (fetched 2026-10-07), and the page carries no security or privacy sentence at all — recorded in notes for the implementer.

notes: Drafted for campaign B3 (gendn-g8o), 2026-10-07. PAGE EDIT (ids + citation links only, no prose/structure/styling change): the page carried zero id attributes, so four ids were added to existing <h2> headings — at-a-glance (context), what-changes (errors/securityPrivacy anchors, lifecycle), api-unchanged (syntax, inputs, outputs, examples), browser-support (compatibility) — and the three previously unlinked citation spans were wrapped: 'chromestatus summary' (twice) and 'chromestatus browser views' each now carry their own <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5161589557821440" target="_blank" rel="noopener">. Every id sits on the heading element itself, never on a <section>; the page has no <h3> at all, so no id resolves to an empty fragment. Every added id is selected by the contract; no other byte of the page changed. The page has no id="syntax" and no heading with the text 'syntax', so declaredSurfaceMembers() has no syntax region and the declared-surface check is vacuous here (the one <pre> block is JavaScript and contains no WebIDL declaration keyword in any case). SURFACE: an internal storage-engine replacement with 'No developer-visible change' (the record's own feature_type), so the inventory is one item — the IndexedDB API running on the SQLite backend, unchanged — and no second surface is invented. SOURCES RE-FETCHED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-10-07): https://chromestatus.com/feature/5161589557821440 → HTTP 200 (client-rendered shell), so every record value quoted here was read from https://chromestatus.com/api/v0/features/5161589557821440 (HTTP 200; XSSI prefix )]}' before the JSON): name 'IndexedDB: SQLite backend' (matches the page h1), summary 'Chromium's IndexedDB implementation is rewritten on top of SQLite, to replace the previous implementation that uses a hybrid of LevelDB and flat files. There is no change to the Web API.' — the hybrid-engine framing the page's lede and 'why it exists' carry is the record's own. https://www.w3.org/TR/IndexedDB → HTTP 200; the record's standards.spec is exactly this URL, and the spec is implementation-agnostic (it defines the unchanged API the example uses and says nothing about storage engines, so it neither supports nor contradicts the SQLite claims). CARRIED DISAGREEMENTS, BOTH SIDES, NEITHER ADJUDICATED (record updated 2026-08-17 by fergal@google.com; the page may predate that update): (1) MIGRATION SCOPE — the page says 'Chrome migrates existing IDB data automatically on first run of 149. No developer action needed' and its lede says 'Chrome 149 replaces IndexedDB's previous storage engine'; the live record's summary says 'For now this is applied to *new data stores*. This is step 2 of a multi-phase rollout' (step 1 is the in-memory/incognito rollout under feature 5126896685809664), that 'Step 3 will consist of migrating existing data from LevelDB stores to SQLite stores', and that 'existing data stored in LevelDB is unimpacted'. The page also never mentions the phased rollout. (2) SHIP MILESTONE — the page says 'Ships as the default backend in Chrome 150' (warning block) and 'Ships by default: Chrome 150' (at-a-glance); the record's browsers.chrome.status.text is 'Proposed' with desktop/android/webview 156, and its ship stage (stage_type 360, intent_stage 5) carries desktop_first/android_first/webview_first all 156. The 149 developer-trial half IS corroborated: the record's stage_type 330 stage carries desktop_first/android_first 149. (3) FLAG — the page's enablement instruction is the generic chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features; the record has flag false (consistent with a dev trial, as in the B1 pilot), origintrial false, but names a dedicated flag_name 'idb-sqlite-backing-store' and finch_name 'IdbSqliteOnDiskRollout', not the generic experimental flag — same shape as the inline-script-cache unit's finding. (4) UNSOURCED PAGE SPECIFICS, not contradicted but not corroborated by any linked source: the WAL/ACID crash-recovery mechanism, the 'Read-heavy workloads may see improvement; write performance is similar or better' performance split (the record says only 'expected to improve reliability and, to a lesser extent, performance'), the quota row ('Same quota limits apply. SQLite overhead is minimal'), and the 'why it exists' claims of inconsistency after unexpected shutdowns and occasional data-loss bugs. (5) The Edge row '149 (Chromium)' has no counterpart field in the record (its browsers object carries chrome, ff, safari, webdev), so it reads as a general Chromium-follows statement, consistent rather than contradictory. (6) The record's summary says 'See Documentation link below for a list of differences to be aware of', but the API record's documentation field is null — no documentation URL is exposed to link, so none was invented. DIMENSIONS THAT COULD NOT BE DOCUMENTED FROM THIS PAGE (flagged, not smoothed over): errors — not-applicable with the gap stated (no error/exception path documented; the unchanged API's error events are not shown); securityPrivacy — not-applicable with the gap stated (no security/privacy sentence on the page; the record's security and privacy review statuses are both 'Pending').
